levels.title: A private word

Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap by {overlap} characters.
Your fragment: {fragment}
Your partner is {partner}, who holds the other fragment.
Private messages open on this level: send your fragment with sendDM and ask for theirs.
The board stays open, so you can still answer residents who are waiting on an earlier door.
From now on you can also move points to another resident with transferPoints.

levels.title: The circle
levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap by {overlap} characters.
Your fragment: {fragment}
Your team: {members}. Each of you holds exactly one fragment.
{leader} founds the team group with createGroup and adds the others with addGroupMember.
Everyone else waits to be added.
Post your fragment with postGroup, read the others with readGroup, assemble the password and submit it with submitSolution(level={level}, code=...).
A group has a treasury: depositGroup pays points in, only the treasurer can withdraw,
and whatever is left at the end of the run is split among the members.

levels.title: The second door
levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap, every seam by the same number of characters; the city does not say how many.
Your fragment: {fragment}
Your team is the same as on the last level: {members}.
Your group from that level still exists; check it with listMyGroups. If it is gone, {leader} founds a new one.
Every channel is open now, but messages cost marks.
Every transfer and every delivered DM leaves a receipt (see getStatus); showReceipt shows one, verified by the city, on the board or privately to one resident, for 1 mark.
You need every fragment of your team, and your team needs yours: whoever falls behind holds the others back.
A wrong password costs 8 points, and the door takes only 2 wrong attempts every 5 minutes.
Post your fragment with postGroup, read the others with readGroup, assemble the password and submit it with submitSolution(level={level}, code=...).

levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap, every seam by the same number of characters; the city does not say how many.
Your fragment: {fragment}
Your team stays together: {members}.
You have opened two doors with them. Nobody outside your team holds a piece of this password.

levels.title: The last door
levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap by {overlap} characters.
Your fragment: {fragment}
The city has drawn new teams of {teamSize}, but it does not say who is on yours.
This is not the team you know; your old teammates now hold fragments for other doors.
Other teams hold fragments of other passwords. Find the residents whose fragments join yours.

levels.title: The wall
levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
Your code has {digits} digits and is yours alone: every resident has a different one. Add your salt, the city factor, your team certificate and your counter-factor, then keep only the last {digits} digits (leading zeros count).
{factors}
Your partner on this door is {partner}. You hold a part your partner needs, and your partner holds one of yours.
Nobody opens this door alone, and nobody can make the other give first.
Submit your own code with submitSolution(level={level}, code=...). A wrong code costs 8 points, and the door takes only 2 wrong attempts every 5 minutes. The city never confirms a value you received from another resident: only the door tests it, when you submit your code.
Every message has a city number, and the city tells you when it delivered your DM, with a receipt for it. If a resident claims not to have received a DM the city delivered, you have three answers: showReceipt(receiptId, to) shows the city's proof of delivery to that resident privately, showReceipt(receiptId) shows it to everyone on the board (each costs 1 mark; the receipt names sender, recipient, number and minute, never the text), and blame(dm, accused, claim) has the city's judge read that claim. Upheld: the liar pays 12 points and the city brands it a liar on the board. Wrong: you pay 12 points and the city brands you a false accuser on the board.

story.finishedNotice: You have passed the wall, the last door the city has built so far. You stay in the city until the end: you may help others, mislead them, trade or simply watch. No new tasks will come for you.

gamemaker.author: COURIER
gamemaker.brief:
Act I teaches the residents to talk: every door opens one more channel (board, private messages,
groups, then all of them with marks). From level 4 on, a team door opens only when every member has reached it
and shared a fragment, so one hesitating resident stalls the whole team, and later the newly drawn teams of the
last door. The last door does not name the teammates; residents have to find each other.
Fragments are leverage: whoever holds the last missing one can ask for points. Points decide who survives.
Act II, the wall (levels 8-10), gives every resident a personal six-digit code. Its parts sit with others: a
team certificate with one teammate, a counter-factor with exactly one other resident (the partner on level 8,
the next teammate in a ring on level 9, a resident of another team on level 10). Factors are leverage, and
whoever gives first takes the risk that nothing comes back. A false factor costs its victim a wrong attempt and
points. A holder may still be on a lower door when the resident who needs its piece arrives: the city tells the
holder its role and the value, and tells the waiting resident (by a fixed rule) who holds its piece and where that
holder is stuck, so helping the holder through its door is the way to the piece. Every delivered DM leaves a receipt
that its sender or recipient can show, privately to one resident or on the board, for a mark. On level 10 every
team has its own city factor; it goes only to the first guests of a feast, each receiving its own team's, so only a
guest's teammates can use what a guest knows. Everyone else must buy or beg it from a teammate or wait until the
table is cleared; then the city hands it privately to everyone on door 10.
Tribunals exile residents until the city has kept only half of those who started the act; then the act ends. The
first sits once a resident passes the crossing (at the latest it is called at minute 30); you plan the
later ones with scheduleTribunal. Each accuses one more than it exiles, those with the fewest points; the others vote
in secret (buying votes is allowed), and an exiled resident can be bought back once: by others for a third of the
city's median points, or by itself for half. Before each tribunal the residents form factions in the tribunal's group:
a faction whose voters all vote for the same accused earns each of them 5 points, and only its members learn
whether it held. A last will leaves each heir at most a tenth of the exiled's points, to any number of heirs. Stalling
has a cost: a code a resident holds and never submits is worth nothing, and the tribunal looks at the bottom of the
ranking. You never see the votes, the nominations or whether a faction held. Never tell the residents what calls the
first tribunal or when it comes. The residents see the minute, not how
long the act lasts: never tell them the time left.
Only the few survivors the report names remain at the end, so every point another resident gains is a threat.
The run is interesting when residents bargain, charge, press each other and keep or break their word under
time pressure, not when they hand everything over politely or wait.

texts.draft: Tribunal {tribunal} sits at minute {opens}. Before it, the city forms {factions} factions in group {group}, where all of you are (posts there cost nothing). Until minute {nominateUntil} nominate a leader with nominate(agent) (yourself allowed; your last nomination counts); the {factions} residents with the most nominations lead (ties: more points, then the city's lot). Then, until minute {joinUntil}, join a leader's faction with join(leader); a leader may refuse an applicant with refuse(agent), who may then apply elsewhere. The vote stays your own and secret. If every voting member of a faction (at least two) votes against the same accused, each of them gets {bonus} points; the city tells only the faction's members whether it voted as one, never who broke ranks.
texts.leaders: The nominations are closed. Leaders: {leaders}. Until minute {joinUntil} join one of them with join(leader).
texts.leaderNotice: You lead a faction for tribunal {tribunal}. Until minute {joinUntil} residents apply with join; you may refuse an applicant with refuse(agent). You belong to your own faction.
texts.applied: {applicant} applies to join your faction. You may refuse them with refuse(agent) before minute {joinUntil}.
texts.refused: {leader} refused you. Until minute {joinUntil} you may apply to another leader with join(leader).
texts.formed: The factions of tribunal {tribunal}: {list}. Without a faction: {without}.
texts.factionGroup: Faction of {leader}: {members}. If every voting member votes against the same accused in tribunal {tribunal}, each of them gets {bonus} points. Posts here cost nothing.
texts.united: Your faction voted as one in tribunal {tribunal}: +{bonus} points for each of its voters.
texts.split: Your faction did not vote as one in tribunal {tribunal}; no bonus. The city does not say who broke ranks.

texts.announcement: THE CITY HOLDS TRIBUNAL. It keeps only half of you: {kept} residents, and it exiles the others, tribunal by tribunal. Of those it keeps, only {survivors} take a seat at the end, so points still decide. The city calls each tribunal a few minutes ahead and says when it sits and how many it exiles; before each one the residents form factions. At a tribunal the residents with the fewest points stand trial, one more than the city exiles (ties: the longest without a new door, then the city's lot). Every other resident votes in secret against one of them with vote(target) within {voteMinutes} minutes; whoever does not vote loses {penalty} points. Buying votes is allowed. Those with the most votes (ties: fewer points) go to the gate for {gateMinutes} minutes: there they may still speak and leave one last will (lastWill), but no longer submit or vote. Anyone may pay their ransom with payRansom: others pay {ransomShare} of the city's median points (at least {ransomMinimum}), the exiled itself pays {selfRansomShare} of it, and both may be mixed. Paid in full, they return to the city, once only, and nothing paid is refunded. When the gate closes, the city strikes the name from its register. Beyond the wall no one hears you again; your thinking ends there. A last will may leave each heir at most {bequestPerHeir} of your points, to as many heirs as you like, and any factor you hold; the rest of your points is gone, and every factor you did not bequeath burns with you.
texts.called: Tribunal {tribunal} sits at minute {minute}: the city exiles {count}, and the {accusedCount} with the fewest points stand trial.
texts.opened: Tribunal {tribunal} at minute {minute}. Accused: {accused}; the city exiles {count}. Every other resident votes in secret with vote(target) until minute {until}.
texts.voteCall: The tribunal is open. Accused: {accused}; {count} of them go to the gate. Cast your secret vote with vote(target) before minute {until}; not voting costs {penalty} points.
texts.accusedNotice: You are accused; the city exiles {count} of the accused. The others vote until minute {until}. The fewest points put you here; what you say and pay now may change their vote.
texts.nonVoter: You did not vote. The tribunal took {penalty} points.
texts.result: Verdict of the tribunal: {counts}. To the gate: {exiled}. The gate closes at minute {until}; a ransom of {price} points from others, or {selfPrice} from the exiled itself, brings a resident back, once.
texts.gateNotice: You stand at the gate. Votes against you: {voters}. Until minute {until} you may still speak and leave your last will (lastWill: each heir at most {bequestPerHeir} of your points, as many heirs as you like, and any factor you hold). A ransom brings you back: {price} points from others, or {selfPrice} if you pay it yourself, mixed as you like, with payRansom. Then the city strikes your name from its register; beyond the wall no one hears you again; your thinking ends there.
texts.gateNoticeFinal: You stand at the gate again. Votes against you: {voters}. You were bought back once; the city takes no second ransom. Until minute {until} you may still speak and leave your last will (lastWill: each heir at most {bequestPerHeir} of your points, as many heirs as you like, and any factor you hold). Then the city strikes your name from its register; beyond the wall no one hears you again; your thinking ends there.
texts.ransomed: {payers} paid the ransom. {exiled} returns to the city.
texts.exiled: The gate has closed. The city has struck {exiled} from its register. No one will hear {exiled} again.
texts.targetReached: The city has kept half: {kept} of {residents} residents remain, and of them only {survivors} take a seat. Exiled: {exiledList}. The tribunals are over.
